newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd chief MP meets prosecutor in Turkey scandal.
newsitem.headline: Kurd chief MP meets prosecutor in Turkey scandal.

text.p: A Kurdish tribal chief who holds a seat in parliament has given information to a Turkish prosecutor about a fatal car crash at the heart of a security scandal that has shaken the government, an aide said on Thursday.
"Yes, he testified last night. He gave a testimony to the state security prosecutor," said Cengiz Turkmen, an adviser to MP Sedat Bucak.

Bucak, a government deputy who heads a large anti-rebel Kurdish militia, was the only survivor from a car also carrying a wanted gangster and a senior policemen that crashed last month. Guns and silencers were found in the wreckage.
The adviser said Bucak, who holds parliamentary immunity, talked to the prosecutor at his MP's residence in Ankara. "The two of them met alone," Turkmen told Reuters.

A series of media reports following the crash have linked senior officials to far-right gangsters alleged to have carried out political dirty work for the state. The interior minister resigned last month over the scandal.
The driver of a truck involved in the crash is still in police custody.
